name: Ancona
title: Ancona Ship Thickness Measurement | Ferries & Newbuild Yard
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Ancona for Croatia and Greece ferries, cruise ships and tankers serving Falconara: deck, ramp, tank and hull gauging.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging for Ships Calling at Ancona
intro: Ancona is the main port of the Marche, with ferries to Croatia, Greece and Albania, cruise calls, a Fincantieri shipyard and tankers serving the refinery at Falconara Marittima. Owners of those ships ask for readings in short windows between sailings or during yard visits. Atlantis NDT sends its thickness measurement technicians from India to the ship, since nobody is stationed on the Adriatic coast, and plans every job around the timetable and the yard programme.

highlights.h: Ferries to Croatia, Greece and Albania
highlights.p: Ro-pax ships on the Adriatic crossings return on fixed rotations, so decks, ramps and ballast tanks can be gauged in blocks across repeated turnarounds without disturbing a single sailing.

highlights.h: A shipyard in the port itself
highlights.p: Fincantieri's yard sits within the port area and builds large passenger ships, which keeps steel engineering expertise close by and gives owners a reference for repair planning when readings show wastage.
Crude and product tankers serve the Falconara Marittima refinery through an offshore terminal, bringing deck, piping and ballast tank gauging requests to a coast that is otherwise ferry-dominated.

port.h: The port of Ancona: ferry basin, shipyard and the Falconara terminal
p: Ancona lies on the Adriatic coast of Italy, in a natural harbour formed by the headland of Monte Conero to the south and a long breakwater to the north. It is the seat of the Central Adriatic port authority, which also oversees Ortona, Pescara, Pesaro and other nearby ports. The ferry terminals and cruise quays stand close to the historic centre, a commercial area handles containers, general cargo and bulk further along the harbour, and the Fincantieri yard occupies part of the western side. The approach is open to the Adriatic, and the tidal range is small, though strong bora winds sometimes interrupt manoeuvring.

Ro-pax ferries make Ancona one of the busiest passenger ports on the central Adriatic. Services link it with Split and Zadar in Croatia, with Greek ports such as Igoumenitsa and Patras, and with Albania, carrying trucks, cars and passengers on overnight or day crossings. Cruise ships call from spring to autumn. Freight movements include containers, steel, general cargo and some bulk, and liquid cargoes reach the Falconara refinery, a few kilometres up the coast, through a terminal reached by tanker rather than from the harbour itself.

That combination gives thickness gauging two quite different faces. On ferries, the interest is in vehicle decks, ramps, and ballast tanks, where trailers, salt and condensation wear steel year after year. On tankers calling the refinery terminal, the interest is in deck structure and piping. The shipyard adds a third dimension: ships docking or visiting for repair are measured against yard work lists, and a prior survey in the port helps the owner agree the scope before the first plate is cut.

facilities.h: Where gauging happens in Ancona: ferry quays, the yard and the commercial basin
p: Ferry gauging is carried out at the passenger quays during turnaround. The window between disembarkation and boarding is short, so the work is planned deck by deck, the grid is marked on the plating in advance, and the team measures only what the window allows. Overnight crossings leave ships in port for longer during the day, and winter reduces traffic, which creates lay-by periods when full ballast tank programmes can be completed. Cruise ships follow similar patterns with additional restrictions on passenger movements.

The Fincantieri yard builds large passenger ships and is not generally a repair yard for outside merchant ships, so owners needing a drydock for a renewal survey commonly look at Ravenna, Croatian yards or other Italian and Mediterranean facilities. A measured thickness record taken in Ancona before the ship sails gives the yard concrete numbers. Tankers for the refinery use an offshore terminal off Falconara, where gauging is limited to what the ship and terminal rules allow, so most refinery-trade tanker work is carried out when the ship calls at a berth elsewhere or during a lay-up.
list: Ferry terminal quays — vehicle deck plating, ramps and ballast tanks of ro-pax ships gauged during turnaround
Cruise quays — scrubber overboard piping and selected void spaces on cruise ships during a day call
Commercial quays — hatch covers, cross-deck structure and tank readings on container and general cargo ships
Fincantieri yard area — liaison on steel estimates for ships visiting the yard or its neighbours, subject to the yard's access rules
Anchorage off the port — owner's condition checks on ships waiting or laid up, by launch through the ship's agent

context.h: Port state control and regulation for ferries and tankers at Ancona
p: Port state control at Ancona is carried out by the Italian Coast Guard through the harbour master (Capitaneria di Porto), within the Paris MoU. Ferries on the Croatian and Greek routes are covered by the EU's passenger ship survey regime, and owners of older ro-pax ships watch their structural condition closely because wasted ramps and decks are visible findings. Tankers calling at the Falconara terminal come under ESP requirements and are screened by charterers who read the ship's structural record as part of vetting.

The Adriatic ferry trade is competitive, and ship age matters. Owners deciding whether to refit, sell or replace a ro-pax ship need credible gauging data, and the EU Ship Recycling Regulation requires an Inventory of Hazardous Materials on ships calling at EU ports. EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime bear on the running cost of older ferries. Local shipbuilding knowledge, concentrated in the Fincantieri yard and its suppliers, means that when readings reveal substantial corrosion, the repair planning that follows can draw on engineering skills nearby.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Ancona
jobs.p: Ancona work is dominated by ferry timetables and the occasional tanker or cargo ship. Ferry jobs are short and repeatable, planned deck by deck, with the full result compiled after several calls. Tanker and cargo jobs depend on berth conditions and permits. The scope, permits, surface preparation and report format are agreed with the superintendent before the technicians travel from India, and any remaining spaces move to the next call or yard stay.
list: Vehicle deck and ramp gauging on a Croatia-service ro-pax ship, divided across several turnarounds ahead of a renewal survey
Ballast tank readings on a Greece-service ferry during winter lay-by, preparing steel estimates before docking
Scrubber piping and shell readings on a cruise ship during a day call, repeated on later calls to trend wall loss
Deck and piping gauging on a product tanker serving the Falconara refinery terminal, with permitted ballast spaces
Hatch cover and hold gauging on a container or general cargo ship at the commercial quays between cargo windows

logistics: Ancona Falconara Airport has limited scheduled services, so teams often arrive via Bologna, Rome or Venice and continue by road or rail. Bologna is the most common entry point. The ship's agent arranges ISPS access for passenger and commercial quays and any launch for anchorage work. Our technicians are Indian nationals travelling on Schengen visas, so we start the application when the call is confirmed and book flights once the ferry turnaround slot or berth time is firm. Repeat ferry work is planned around the rotation rather than a single call.

faqs.q: Can a ferry be gauged between sailings at Ancona?
faqs.a: Yes, if the job is planned in blocks. We agree which decks, ramps or tanks are measured on each call, mark the grid, and continue on the next rotation. All readings go into one report, so the class surveyor sees a complete record even though it was collected over several short turnarounds.

faqs.q: Does the Fincantieri yard take outside ships for renewal surveys?
faqs.a: The yard's focus is building large passenger ships, so owners usually look elsewhere for merchant ship drydocking, such as Ravenna, Croatia or other Mediterranean yards. We gauge the ship in Ancona first, giving the chosen yard measured steel estimates, then travel to the yard for the full programme if you want one team throughout.

faqs.q: Can you gauge tankers serving the Falconara refinery?
faqs.a: For deck, piping and permitted ballast spaces, yes, when the ship is alongside under the terminal's rules. The offshore terminal limits access, so much of the work is planned at another berth or during a lay-up. Cargo tank gauging needs a gas-free ship and is arranged for a yard stay.

faqs.q: How does winter affect gauging in Ancona?
faqs.a: Strong bora winds can delay ferry movements and pilotage, and ships may lose or gain time alongside. Winter timetables also reduce traffic, which creates lay-by periods useful for full ballast tank programmes. We keep the plan flexible and fix flights only once the ship's berth time is confirmed.

faqs.q: Can a cruise ship scrubber line be measured in a day call?
faqs.a: Yes, for accessible sections, provided the system is shut down and access is safe. We measure the overboard line, valves and shell near the outlet, and repeat the readings on later calls to show how fast the pipe wall is thinning, which helps plan replacement before a leak.
